Article Title: EPFO approves Systematic Withdrawal Plan; retirees can now withdraw PF savings in regular instalments
Article Text:
According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement.

What is EPFO’s SWP for your PF account?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a big move that will benefit lakhs of provident fund subscribers, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ). The Times of India had first reported about the proposal being under consideration today. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time instead of taking out the entire amount at once.The SWP is intended to help members turn their retirement savings into a regular and predictable source of income while retaining ownership of the underlying corpus, according to an ANI report quoting EPFO.At present, members are required to withdraw their entire provident fund corpus within three years of retirement to avoid their accounts becoming inoperative and ceasing to earn annual interest.If a member dies while receiving payments, the nominee or dependent will have the option of withdrawing the remaining balance or continuing to receive periodic payouts.According to the EPFO, the initiative will strengthen financial security after retirement by offering a flexible and dependable income stream while protecting the interests of members’ families.The plan would give crores of existing subscribers access to the facility as well, particularly those who find it difficult to manage their retirement savings prudently.The proposal was discussed at a meeting of the central board of trustees on Thursday, chaired by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya.According to the TOI report, in its initial phase, the voluntary scheme is expected to focus on existing EPFO subscribers. The organisation estimates that around 6.3 lakh members aged above 55 years could benefit from the facility at the outset.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) has approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation. Under the proposed facility, members will be able to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in instalments over a period of time.

Article Title: Nvidia Q3 results: Revenue jumps 103% to $115.8 billion; announces $0.25 per-share dividend
Article Text:
Nvidia delivers blockbuster Q3

Nvidia Q3 results

Jensen Huang admits mistakes, signals willingness to return

Board refuses to bring back Huang

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia Q3 results: Nvidia investors finally have something to cheer about as the chipmaker reported a blockbuster third quarter, with revenue soaring more than 100% year-on-year.The company reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, marking a 103% increase from the year-ago period and a 20% rise from the previous quarter. Its GAAP earnings per diluted share stood at $2.70, while non-GAAP earnings per diluted share came in at $2.68.The timing of the results is particularly significant as the tech giant is caught up in a series of controversies surrounding its former boss, Jensen Huang, alleged to have had a relationship with a Chinese ‘spy’, apart from two other women.Also Read| As Nvidia founder Jensen Hunag says, he is ready to come back as CEO; Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says board has determined it will not reinstate Huang and that is Board's The company reported GAAP gross margins of 74.8% and non-GAAP gross margins of 74.9% for the quarter. Nvidia also returned $28.1 billion to shareholders during the third quarter of fiscal 2027 through share buybacks and cash dividends.Back in September 2026, Nvidia's Board of Directors approved an additional $150 billion in share repurchase authorisation, with no expiration date. At the end of the third quarter, approximately $227.3 billion remained available under the programme.Nvidia's next quarterly cash dividend will be $0.25 per share, payable on December 23, 2026, to shareholders on record as of December 2, 2026.Commenting on the quarterly performance, Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of Nvidia, highlighted the company's continued momentum and technology leadership.“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in a press statement.She also expressed confidence in the company's technology roadmap, adding, “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater."While Nvidia's financial performance remained in focus, former CEO Jensen Huang made his first public comments since being caught up in the alleged Chinese Spy Scandal.In a statement on X, Huang thanked those who had supported him and his family over the past week. He also spoke about his journey to the United States and described becoming an American citizen as one of the proudest moments of his life."Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life."Huang described Nvidia as his life's work and said building the company alongside his colleagues had been a privilege. He also acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected at the company and said he regretted the difficulties caused to its board."Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honour. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he added.His statement also signalled his willingness to return as the company's chief executive if the board backed his reinstatement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said.However, any possibility of Huang returning to the leadership role was ruled out by Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones. Speaking at the beginning of the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, Jones said the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and had no intention of bringing him back as CEO."The board of directors unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said.The chairman's remarks came just hours after Huang indicated that he would be open to returning to the company if invited.The controversy centres on Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese Spy. The former CEO resigned last week following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a Chinese woman who worked at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.The allegations have also brought scrutiny to relationships linked to Huang both within and outside Nvidia. His latest statement acknowledged personal mistakes and expressed his commitment to cooperating with the board's independent investigation.
Article Summary: N Nvidia reports blockbuster third quarter, with revenue soaring more than 100% year-on-year. Company reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, marking a 103% increase from the year-ago period. Former CEO Jensen Huang made his first public comments since being caught up in the alleged Chinese Spy Scandal. Huang acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected at the company and said he regretted the difficulties caused to its board.

Article Title: Anthropic surpasses SpaceX with record $81.31 billion IPO, prices shares at $83 apiece
Article Text:
Anthropic makes blockbuster debut at stock market

Heavy spending makes fresh capital important

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Anthropic has emerged with the biggest IPO ever, raising $81.31 billion through its stock-market offering and surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising. The artificial intelligence company priced its shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday (local time), above its initially indicated range of $70-$78.The pricing values the San Francisco-based AI company at $1.5 trillion and reflects strong investor demand despite concerns surrounding the technology sector and the possibility of an AI bubble.Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI tool, is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT". While its initial plan was to offer 825 million shares, the final offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock.Of the total, 956,351,354 shares are being sold by Anthropic itself, while 23,648,646 shares are being offered by certain existing stockholders.The scale of investor interest comes at a time when the market is dealing with several uncertainties. These include the ouster of Nvidia's CEO, concerns about an AI bubble, the possibility of a regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public.Despite these concerns, Anthropic's pricing indicates that investors remain willing to put money into major AI companies.“This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia. The pricing shows strong demand among investors,” said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co.Its rival OpenAI, meanwhile, is not planning to enter the stock market until next year.Beyond setting an IPO record, the fundraising gives Anthropic an opportunity to secure additional capital without adding to its existing debt burden.The company has already borrowed $6.2 billion, an amount it has described as “substantial” in its financial filings. It is also unprofitable under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to service interest and principal payments are limited.Its financial requirements are particularly significant given the scale of its infrastructure commitments. Anthropic has signed leases and other agreements that will require it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years. Of this, $70 billion is due to be spent over the next 12 months.Although the company currently has ample cash, its sizeable spending plans mean those reserves could be used up quickly if it cannot secure additional funding.
Article Summary: Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI tool, is scheduled to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT" The company has signed leases and other agreements that will require it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure over the coming years.

Article Title: Household savings must go not just to equity but all parts of life-cycle capital : Dipam Secretary
Article Text:
Household savings must go not just to equity but all parts of life-cycle capital

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) secretary Arunish Chawla has called for a restructuring of India's financing ecosystem to channel household savings into a wider range of assets, mobilise pension and insurance funds for long-term investment, deepen fixed-income markets and expand domestic participation in alternative investment funds. He has argued that policy, tax and regulatory frameworks need to evolve to direct capital towards the financing requirements of Viksit Bharat.Addressing the CII DFS Financing Summit 2026, he said household savings had traditionally been concentrated in real estate, gold and valuables rather than financial assets. Changing this pattern would require policy, regulatory and tax incentives to bring more household savings into the formal financial system. "The question is how we can incentivize a behavioral change through policy, through regulation, through tax incentives, in a way that ordinary Indians, working Indians, saving Indians become part of our formalized financial economy and help enhance growth and also finance the financing needs of a Viksit Bharat in both public and private sectors," he said.He said the expansion of demat accounts and mutual fund assets showed the growing participation of households in capital markets.Demat accounts had increased from around 3.6 crore in 2019 to 25 crore in Oct 2026, while mutual fund assets under management had risen from Rs 15 lakh crore in 2016 to Rs 84 lakh crore.However, he said financialisation of household savings needed to extend beyond equity markets to finance companies at different stages of their life cycle. "Household savings... can be channeled and recycled to not just our equity markets, but all parts of our life-cycle capital," he said.Another challenge was the imbalance between equity and fixed-income markets. While India's market capitalisation ranked among the four or five largest globally, the development of bond markets remained important to provide companies with alternatives to equity financing. "How we develop the bond side, the fixed-income side of our markets, and how we incentivize it vis-à-vis equity is going to be another very big challenge into the next 20 years," he said.He also called for a greater role for market-based financing in meeting long-term investment requirements, arguing that banks, given the structure of their deposits and lending, were primarily suited to medium-term financing. Pension and insurance funds, whose assets were growing, could provide a source of long-term capital.The DIPAM secretary also called for expanding domestic participation in alternative investment funds (AIFs), including venture capital and private equity. He said the AIF industry, with cumulative investments of Rs 7.5 lakh crore, was around one-tenth the size of the mutual fund industry, whose cumulative investments stood at Rs 84 lakh crore.
Article Summary: DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla has called for a restructuring of India's financing ecosystem. He argued that policy, tax and regulatory frameworks need to evolve to direct capital towards the financing requirements of Viksit Bharat. He said household savings had traditionally been concentrated in real estate, gold and valuables rather than financial assets.

Article Title: PFRDA looking at ways to incentivise distribution without reducing returns
Article Text:
The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is exploring innovative strategies to boost pension distribution.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: PFRDA is examining ways to improve pension distribution by addressing low distributor commissions, which remain at a fifth of mutual fund industry levels despite a 2.5-fold increase. The regulator is also reviewing investment allocation to improve long-term returns, including greater exposure to growth assets and alternative investment funds, PFRDA chairman S Ramann said.Pension distributors receive a fifth of the commissions available to mutual fund distributors despite PFRDA having increased the distributable commission pool 2.5 times. Ramann said low commissions were one of the reasons pension products had failed to gain wider acceptance. "We actually have a bit of an inverse problem as compared to the insurance industry where we have money on the table for the distributors is so abysmally low that it's one of the reasons why probably the pension product never really went out in a big way.So, even after having increased the total sort of distributable commissions that lie on the table two and a half times, we're still one-fifth the commission's level which is available in the mutual fund industry," he said.He was speaking at the Gatekeepers of Governance 2026 event in Mumbai.The regulator is also weighing the need to balance distributor incentives with the cost borne by subscribers over the long term. Ramann said commissions on pension products needed to be assessed over their long investment horizon, which could extend to 30 or 50 years. "Over that period of time, we should probably count the compounding effect of that commission also. And that's really when we start getting into this conflict of what should be a fair commission or a total cost to the customer," he said.The regulator has set up two expert committees to examine asset allocation, one under former SBI chairman Dinesh Khara and another headed by investment expert Narayan Ramachandran, who has worked with mutual funds.Ramann said the committees had provided inputs on whether pension savings were being allocated to the appropriate asset classes to generate returns for retirement payouts. He cited Australia's superannuation programme, the equivalent of India's defined contribution pension system, where 72% of the corpus is invested in growth assets, with around 28% in fixed income. Nearly half of the growth-asset allocation is in unlisted investments.India's pension ecosystem remains risk-averse, with inadequate capital flowing into greenfield projects and startups, Ramann said. NPS has started its own fund of funds to invest in AIFs, allowing pension savings to gain exposure to a diversified pool of investments. "It is citizens' money going into the AIFs, so that they get a respectable and a better sort of diversified return," he said.On pension payouts, PFRDA is examining the possibility of introducing a market-based guarantee mechanism for private-sector subscribers. A committee headed by Sahu is studying the proposal, though Ramann said guarantees would involve costs. "Our job is to look at it, look at the future, see what we can build in baby steps maybe," he said.
Article Summary: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) is exploring innovative strategies to boost pension distribution. The regulator is also reviewing investment allocation to improve long-term returns. PFRDA chairman S Ramann said low commissions were one of the reasons pension products had failed to gain wider acceptance.

Article Title: IRDAI flags conflict in banks, auto dealers selling insurance
Article Text:
Ajay Seth, the chairman of IRDAI, advocates for enhanced corporate governance within the insurance industry to mitigate conflicts of interest.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: IRDAI chairman has called for stronger corporate governance in the insurance sector, citing potential conflicts of interest when lenders sell insurance and automobile dealers combine insurance distribution with vehicle repair services. He also called for boards to act as the first gatekeepers of governance, drawing on RBI's engagement with bank and NBFC boards. Separately, he questioned whether financial regulators should erect barriers between sectors or allow savings to move towards more efficient managers, while flagging risks from the widespread use of AI in insurance underwriting and claims settlement.Speaking at the Gatekeepers of Governance 2026 event in Mumbai helmed by former Sebi chief M Damodaran, Ajay Seth, chairman of IRDAI, said business models that had served the industry for decades could also create conflicts of interest. He said boards needed to establish safeguards to ensure these conflicts did not compromise customer interests."Some business models have served very well over decades, but that brings in the associated risks in terms of conflict of interest," Seth said. Citing lenders selling insurance and automobile dealers combining insurance distribution with damage repair services, he said, "These are the two different signs of services.They have to be kept separately rather than mixing with each other."Seth said boards had a responsibility to establish safeguards against such conflicts. "The role of the board becomes more important, that what kind of a guardrail it sets to take care that those conflicts of interest do not come in the way of providing the best advice, best service, best product to the customers," he said.He also called for the insurance sector to strengthen corporate governance by adopting practices followed by RBI in its engagement with banks and NBFCs. He cited RBI's structured interactions with company boards and independent directors as an approach that had helped improve governance across the financial sector.On the movement of household savings between financial products, Seth questioned whether regulators should create barriers between sectors or facilitate the flow of savings towards more efficient managers. He said changing preferences were reshaping the way savings were managed and called for greater coordination among financial regulators."So, as the shift in the economy is taking place in terms of the savings management and the preference of the people are changing, do we build higher and higher walls so that the water doesn't come in? Or we build boats so that we can sail wherever we want to be," he said.Seth also flagged the risks arising from the growing use of artificial intelligence in insurance. "Are those models trained enough for our economy, our behaviour of the policyholders and the associated risks? Are humans in charge of taking the final decision?" he said.
Article Summary: IRDAI chairman Ajay Seth has called for stronger corporate governance in the insurance sector. He cited potential conflicts of interest when lenders sell insurance and automobile dealers combine insurance distribution with vehicle repair services. Seth also questioned whether financial regulators should erect barriers between sectors or allow savings to move towards more efficient managers.

Article Title: Rising tech outages put digital resilience in focus
Article Text:
Error messages on pages for Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft Copilot on a laptop arranged in London, UK, on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Microsoft Corp. is struggling to restore access to its flagship software and end an outage that has paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses globally. Photographer: Chris J. Ratcliffe/Bloomberg

Bengaluru:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Another day, another major technology outage. Over the past week, disruptions have hit Microsoft Outlook and Teams, Cloudflare, AWS, Anthropic’s Claude, Workday, Apple services, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency’s classified network, NSANet.In India, a Microsoft cloud outage disrupted email-based customer support at IndiGo, Air India and Akasa Air, while financial services, telecom and IT companies reported problems accessing corporate email and workplace applications. Flight operations were unaffected. Cloudflare also reported disruptions at multiple Indian locations earlier this month.Apple blamed Tuesday’s outages on an internal update, ruling out a cyberattack. The disruptions affected the App Store, iCloud sign-in, Mail and web apps, with some services down for over four hours. While consumer services were restored by Wednesday, two outages affecting its developer platform, App Store Connect, remained listed.“The most alarming thing about this wave of outages is how a failure in one part of our digital infrastructure can disrupt airlines, banks, governments, and millions of people almost simultaneously,” said Tal Kollender, founder and CEO of Israeli cybersecurity firm Remedio.A single misconfiguration, failed update or broken dependency can trigger widespread disruption, she said. As AI becomes embedded in critical infrastructure, autonomous systems making decisions and changes at speeds humans cannot always control could add to the risks. Cybersecurity must move beyond detecting problems to fixing vulnerabilities, with safeguards to ensure corrective actions do not cause further outages, she added.Diwakar Dayal, managing director and area vice-president, SentinelOne India and SAARC, said the biggest cyber risk was not just a breach but the inability to operate when technology failed.“Digital resilience is becoming a new measure of business leadership. In an interconnected world, a technology failure anywhere can become a business crisis everywhere,” he said. For India, where digital infrastructure underpins banking, aviation, public services and commerce, resilience was an economic and national security imperative. Companies need operational redundancy and the ability to contain disruption and recover quickly, he added.Rahul Sasi, CEO and co-founder of CloudSEK, said even unsuccessful cyber exploitation attempts could disrupt services. “Hackers don’t always need to succeed in breaking into a system to cause damage. Sometimes, even a failed attempt can crash an application or bring down an entire service,” he said, citing PHP2Shell.Some publicly available proof-of-concept exploits could crash servers rather than achieve remote code execution, he said. This, however, does not establish that recent outages were caused by cyberattacks.Rajnish Gupta, managing director and country manager, Tenable India, said there was no evidence that AI-driven attacks caused the Microsoft and Cloudflare outages. However, organisations must assess risks across interconnected systems and third-party platforms.Tenable research found that organisations face an average of three attack paths for every security finding.“Cybersecurity is no longer just about preventing attacks. It is about ensuring businesses can survive them,” Dayal said.
Article Summary: Disruptions have hit Microsoft Outlook and Teams, Cloudflare, AWS, Anthropic’s Claude, Workday, Apple services, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency's classified network, NSANet. A single misconfiguration, failed update or broken dependency can trigger widespread disruption, she said.

Article Title: Man sold house but did not file ITR and on getting tax notice he claimed Rs 49 lakh exemption, but taxman denied it; ITAT Mumbai gives relief saying missing original tax return alone cannot shut the d
Article Text:
In his ITR, the man reported long-term capital gains from the sale of a residential property. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

CIT vs Sun Engineering Works (P.) Ltd.

Why ITAT Mumbai ruled in assessee’s favour

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Can you claim an exemption in your income tax return if you have not filed it originally and only initiate ITR filing after getting a notice from the Income Tax Department In a relief for taxpayers, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled that an exemption claim under Section 54 of the Income Tax (I-T) Act for reinvestment of capital gains in a new house cannot be rejected merely because the taxpayer did not initially file an income tax return.The tribunal held that such a claim can be considered and allowed when it is made during reassessment proceedings.The case concerned an individual taxpayer who had not submitted an original income tax return under Section 139(1).The dispute concerned the assessment year 2017-18. According to the tribunal's order, the Income Tax Department had information that the man purchased an immovable property valued at Rs 45 lakh during the relevant year. Since he had not filed his income tax return, proceedings were initiated under Section 147 of the Income Tax Act. A notice under Section 148 was issued on March 24, 2024.The man filed his return in response to the notice on April 4, 2024. In it, he claimed an exemption under Section 54 on the capital gains from the sale of a residential property. The sale agreement was dated.In his ITR, the man reported long-term capital gains from the sale of a residential property and sought an exemption of Rs 49 lakh under Section 54, citing his investment in another residential property.Section 54 of the Act allows individuals to claim an exemption on long-term capital gains arising from the sale of a residential property to the extent that the gains are reinvested in purchasing another residential house within the stipulated period.The assessing officer turned down the assessee’s claim, citing the absence of an original income tax return.The assessment order referred to Section 54D while disallowing the claim made under Section 54, and added Rs 31,38,256 to his income.The man challenged the addition before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), but the appellate authority upheld the decision. It relied on the Supreme Court's judgment in, which addresses the limits on claims that can be raised during reassessment proceedings.ITAT Mumbai clarified that although reassessment proceedings cannot be used to reopen matters unrelated to income that has escaped assessment, taxpayers can raise claims that have a direct connection with such income.The ITAT observed that the capital gains in this case were themselves the income that had escaped assessment, making the claim for exemption under Section 54 directly relevant to the calculation of that income.The order explains that the escaped income in this case was the long-term capital gain from the sale of a residential property. The Section 54 claim related to the computation of that very income and was not an unrelated claim raised during reassessment.It therefore held that the exemption request could not be classified as a new or unrelated claim that was impermissible during reassessment proceedings.The tribunal also cited earlier judicial rulings which established that Section 54 does not make filing an income tax return by the prescribed due date a mandatory condition for claiming the exemption. It stressed that a claim submitted in a return filed in response to a reassessment notice cannot be turned down simply because it was made late or the taxpayer had not filed an original return.The order also records that, in a case involving the man’s wife, the assessing officer had accepted a Section 54 deduction claimed in a return filed in response to a reassessment notice for the remaining 50% share of the investment in the new property. The tribunal noted this circumstance while considering the man’s argument.In its reasoning, the tribunal stated that the earlier decisions supported allowing the claim to be examined rather than rejecting it solely because no original return had been filed. It concluded: “We thus, respectfully relying on the above judgments are inclined to allow the appeal of the Assessee, therefore, remand the case to the file of the AO for decision afresh on the claim of the Assessee under section 54 of the Act within the parameters and/or conditions set out in section 54 of the Act but not otherwise. ”The ITAT consequently overturned the orders passed by the lower authorities and sent the case back to the assessing officer for fresh consideration.It directed the officer to assess the taxpayer’s entitlement to the Section 54 exemption on merits and grant the benefit if the applicable statutory requirements are met.
Article Summary: The case concerned an individual taxpayer who had not submitted an original income tax return under Section 139(1) The dispute concerned the assessment year 2017-18. In his ITR, the man reported long-term capital gains from the sale of a residential property and sought an exemption of Rs 49 lakh under Section 54. The assessing officer turned down the assessee’s claim.

Article Title: Employee worked 4 years, 9 months and 12 days, not 5 years, and Bengaluru Metro denied him Rs 1.75 lakh gratuity; Karnataka High Court orders full payment with 10% interest after examining the 240-day
Article Text:
The Karnataka High Court observed that the dispute could not be decided simply by checking whether the man had completed five calendar years. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why the court ruled in favour of ex-employee

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Are you entitled to a gratuity payout if you have not completed five years of continuous service with your employer? While the Labour codes have undergone a change and some rules have changed, certain pending cases also raise this important question.In one such case, the Karnataka High Court has ruled that an employee who leaves a job before completing five years of continuous service can still qualify for gratuity if the conditions laid down under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 , are met.The court held that where an employee has worked for at least 240 days during the 12 calendar months immediately preceding his resignation, the period can be treated as a complete year of service for determining gratuity eligibility.The dispute involved a former assistant engineer at Bangalore Metro , whose claim for Rs 1.75 lakh in gratuity was rejected because his tenure fell short of five years.He had worked for four years, nine months and 12 days.The man joined the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation (BMRCL) as an assistant engineer on July 6, 2017. He resigned on March 19, 2022, and was formally relieved of his duties on April 18, 2022. His total period of employment amounted to four years, nine months and 12 days.After leaving the corporation, he made several representations seeking payment of gratuity. He claimed Rs 1.85 lakh, calculating the amount on the basis of his last-drawn monthly salary of Rs 64,210.BMRCL declined to release the payment, prompting him to approach the court.The Karnataka High Court observed that the dispute could not be decided simply by checking whether the man had completed five calendar years from the date he joined BMRCL.His entitlement to gratuity had to be assessed by reading Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act alongside the definition of “continuous service” provided under Sections 2(c) and 2A.The bench also made it clear that gratuity is not a discretionary payment or a benefit granted by an employer as a matter of goodwill, an ET report said. It is a statutory entitlement that becomes payable when the employee fulfils the conditions prescribed under the law.Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act lays down the requirement of five years of continuous service, subject to certain specified exceptions.However, the court said this provision cannot be considered on its own, without taking into account Section 2(c), which defines “continuous service” with reference to Section 2A.Section 2A, in turn, sets out the statutory criteria for determining whether an employee has completed continuous service. Under the circumstances specified in sub-section (2), an employee can be deemed to have completed the prescribed period of continuous service if he has worked for at least 240 days during the relevant 12-calendar-month period.The Karnataka High Court observed that the deeming provision is an integral part of the legal framework for determining continuous service, rather than a factor that can be disregarded.Consequently, an employee’s eligibility cannot be decided merely by counting the calendar time between the date of joining and the end of employment. The actual number of days worked and the applicability of Section 2A of the Payment of Gratuity Act must also be examined.Against this backdrop, the court identified the central issue in the man’s case as whether his employment during the fifth year met the statutory conditions and whether he could claim the benefit of the deeming provision on the basis of the facts placed before the statutory authorities.The Karnataka High Court ruled in favour of the engineer and directed Bangalore Metro to pay him Rs 1.75 lakh along with interest at 10% from May 18, 2022.Explaining the significance of the decision, Mayank Parashar, Legal Associate at Clasis Law-India, told ET: "Karnataka High Court has now re-settled the principle in the context of eligibility of the continuous service requirement for gratuity and concluded that employers should consider the definition of continuous service and key conditions for gratuity together. That’s said every employee who has completed 240 days in 6 days working and 190 days in 5 days working but has not completed the entire year should be considered eligible for gratuity. "
Article Summary: Karnataka High Court ruled that an employee who leaves a job before completing five years of continuous service can still qualify for gratuity. The court held that where an employee has worked for at least 240 days during the 12 calendar months immediately preceding his resignation, the period can be treated as a complete year of service for determining gratuity eligibility.

Nvidia Corp sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of long-time leader Jensen Huang: He's not coming back, and the company will be fine without him.Total sales rose 103% to $115.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The champion of semiconductors for artificial intelligence once again exceeded expectations, both in terms of revenue and net income, which reached $65.3 billion.The chip giant boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve Nvidia's access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Huang might return. The company also added $150 billion to its stock-buyback programme.The shares rose as much as 2.7% to $159.7 on Wednesday after trading got underway in New York. Nvidia's stock has tumbled in recent weeks, battered by the scandal and broader fears that AI spending is poised to slow. It's down about 17% this year."Our supply is growing, our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed," interim CEO Colette Kress said during a conference call with analysts Tuesday."We've got this." It was a high-stakes moment for Kress, who took the reins last week after Huang's ouster - a chaotic exit spurred by multiple extramarital affairs and concerns that he was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot.Nvidia has been the largest beneficiary of the AI build-out, and Huang served as the industry's biggest cheerleader. Now the company looks to ensure that its momentum won't be undermined by the controversy swirling around it."The cards of doubt seemed stacked so high. However, from a bird's-eye view it was a solid 3Q27 print," said Daniel Morgan, a senior portfolio manager at Synovus Trust. "The number of concerns surrounding Nvidia shares will most likely keep the shares range-bound." Bloomberg

Article Title: Anthropic IPO: How to buy shares, expected price and risks investors should know

Anthropic prepares to hit stock market

Anthropic IPO price

How can retail investors apply?

Buying Anthropic through mutual funds

Risks

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

AI giant Anthropic is preparing for its stock market debut, giving individual investors an opportunity to own a stake in the company behind chatbot Claude. The initial public offering (IPO) is expected to value the company at $1.4 trillion (£1 trillion), making it one of the biggest stock market listings in history.Investor demand is already strong, with reports suggesting that the offering is nearly six times oversubscribed. However, the IPO comes amid volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks.Here is what investors need to know about the share price, application process and risks before deciding whether to invest.According to the company's prospectus, Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The final price will be decided on Wednesday.The shares will carry voting rights, but all the votes combined will account for only 49.9% of the total voting power. This means investors will not have enough voting rights to force changes in how the company is run.The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.Investors in the UK can subscribe to Anthropic shares through AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro.The minimum investment differs across platforms.Robinhood and eToro require a minimum investment of $250 (£189), while Hargreaves Lansdown has set the minimum at £250. AJ Bell requires at least £1,000.The application deadlines are 1pm on Wednesday for AJ Bell and 3pm for Hargreaves Lansdown and Robinhood. All three platforms have warned that applications could close earlier without notice.Those who miss the IPO can still buy shares once they begin trading on the Nasdaq. They will also be available through platforms that are not participating in the offering.Direct investment is not the only way to gain exposure to Anthropic. Some funds already hold stakes in the company.In the UK, these include the Baillie Gifford US Growth and Scottish Mortgage investment trusts. Fidelity also has investments in funds available to US investors.After the listing, Anthropic shares are expected to enter some tracker funds, although the timing will vary. Actively managed funds may also choose to buy the stock. This means investors could gain exposure through their existing fund investments without purchasing shares directly.Strong demand does not necessarily mean the shares will deliver lasting returns. Anthropic's prospectus includes 92 pages detailing potential risks to the company and its industry. Recent volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks, is another factor investors need to consider.The company's governance structure has also attracted scrutiny. The Guardian's financial editor Nils Pratley has raised concerns, saying it “represents an extraordinary concentration of power in the hands of a few individuals”.Jason Hollands, managing director of investment platform Bestinvest by Evelyn Partners, which is not participating in the IPO, has also highlighted concerns about the company's profitability.“Anthropic would give most retail investors the first opportunity to have a direct stake in a frontier AI developer. But it remains a capital-intensive business, and it has yet to establish a consistent path to profitability,” he told The Guardian. “Investors will need to judge whether the company can turn demand for its models into durable earnings.”Hollands says strong demand and limited share supply could push up the stock initially, but that does not guarantee sustained gains.
Article Summary: Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.

Article Title: Nepal to buy up to 350 MW power from India as hydropower output falls
Article Text:
Nepal has been granted clearance to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India, a crucial step for winter preparedness. (Pic Credit: Agency)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India has granted Nepal permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity during the winter season to meet its domestic demand. The approval comes as the country’s hydropower generation declined and several power projects remain damaged by recent floods.The central electricity authority (CEA), under India's ministry of power, has authorised the Nepal electricity authority (NEA), the state-owned power utility, to purchase electricity from the Indian energy exchange (IEX) at competitive rates for up to 17 hours daily, NEA officials said.NEA managing direction Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha said that the approval will remain valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027. The move is expected to help Nepal bridge the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic production, according to news agency PTI.Under the approved arrangement, Nepal can import 300 MW through the Kataiya-Kushaha, Ramnagar-Surajpura and Raxaul-Parwanipur transmission lines. An additional 50 MW can be sourced through the new nautanwa-mainahiya transmission line.Nepal's heavy reliance on run-of-the-river hydropower projects makes its electricity production dependent on seasonal changes in river flows.During summer, increased water levels allow the country to generate surplus electricity, much of which is exported to India. However, falling river levels during winter reduce hydropower output, compelling Nepal to depend on electricity imports to meet domestic requirements.The country's power generation capacity has also been affected by damage to several hydropower projects in central Nepal during the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August.Power projects with a combined installed capacity of 431 MW have remained disconnected from the national grid since the disaster, further straining domestic electricity supplies.However, officials expect domestic generation to recover from mid-April as river water levels begin to rise. The improvement could reduce Nepal's reliance on imported electricity and potentially enable the country to resume power exports.
Article Summary: Nepal has been granted permission to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India. The approval comes as the country’s hydropower generation declined and several power projects remain damaged by recent floods. The move is expected to help Nepal bridge the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic production.

The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high on Wednesday as steady retail sales, rising import prices and comments from Federal Reserve officials strengthened expectations of another interest rate hike in December.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged up 0.05% to 103.66 after touching 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025.The euro slipped 0.12% to $1.0984, while the Japanese yen weakened 0.06% to 159.46 per dollar. Oil prices declined on Wednesday after industry data showed a sharp increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although continued hostilities between the United States and Iran and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the fall.US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped 56 cents, or 0.65%, to $85.45 a barrel, while Brent crude futures fell 16 cents, or 0.17%, to $92.98 a barrel as of 1.49 am GMT, according to Reuters.Market sources said US crude stocks increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) released on Tuesday.Gasoline inventories rose by 5.12 million barrels, while distillate stocks increased by 351,000 barrels.The inventory build put pressure on prices, but concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East continued to support the market.Oil benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday as the conflict between Washington and Tehran intensified, despite continuing talks involving Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.Bahrain's defence force said on Wednesday it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.The development followed an exchange of strikes between the US and Iran a day earlier.Iranian drones attacked a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, prompting Washington to strike a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, Reuters reported.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has also faced continued risks. An LPG tanker was hit by a projectile while sailing through the waterway off Oman's coast on Monday, forcing its crew to evacuate.The strait is a key route for global energy shipments, and attacks on vessels have added to concerns over the movement of oil and other fuel supplies.“Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalization of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions,” LSEG analysts said in a note on Tuesday.Supply concerns have also extended beyond the immediate US-Iran confrontation. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group said on Tuesday that it had launched five drones towards two pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.Saudi Arabia has been using the pipeline during the conflict to reroute oil to its Yanbu port for export, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.The latest developments have kept attention on the security of alternative export routes as the conflict continues, even as rising US crude and fuel inventories weigh on prices.

Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones on Tuesday ruled out Jensen Huang's return, saying the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.The company's revenue, meanwhile, soared more than 100% year-on-year."The board of directors unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call.His statement came hours after Huang expressed his desire to return to the company if invited.Huang, who left Nvidia last week following revelations of an extramarital affair and other alleged relationships, made his first public comments since his departure in a social media post. Acknowledging "serious mistakes" in his personal life, he said he would be "honoured" to return if the board believed it was in the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees and the country.His possible return had drawn support from several technology industry figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. US President Donald Trump has also backed his reinstatement, saying the Taiwan-born executive had "learned a big lesson".An online petition urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang has attracted support from current and former employees, investors and other Silicon Valley figures. Its organisers questioned whether his departure had followed due process and called for an independent investigation into the allegations.Meanwhile, Nvidia made no mention of Huang's departure or possible return in its third-quarter earnings statement released on Tuesday.The chipmaker reported revenue of more than $116 billion, double the figure from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates. Net income stood at $2.70 per share, beating analysts' expectations of $2.48.Chief financial officer Colette Kress was expected to address Wall Street analysts on the earnings call for the first time since being named interim CEO following Huang's departure.His exit followed revelation of a relationships with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of having links to Beijing's intelligence services and a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.The businesswoman was an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US investigation for allegedly violating export controls by diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies.
Article Summary: Chairman Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. His statement came hours after Huang expressed his desire to return to the company if invited. Huang left Nvidia last week following revelations of an extramarital affair and other alleged relationships.

Article Title: China, Russia’s reality check for Trump: Why US sanctions may not matter any more
Article Text:
What has changed? Why is the world less affected by US sanctions?

Also check:

How the US built its sanctions power

Diminshing impact of US sanctions power

Fossil Fuel Shipment Departures From Russia

How Northern Sea Route Works For China

Countries with Most Rare Earths

What this means for US

Outstanding foreign official Treasury Holdings

Reaction of 10-year Treasury yield to sanctions

What it means for India

Trump waives Russia-related sanctions for India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For a long time, secondary sanctions have served to be an effective tool for the US. The Donald Trump administration has been aggressively using them in a bid to exercise geoeconomic influence over individuals, businesses and banks linked to countries that it considers as adversaries.In fact, for many years, these measures have proved to be highly effective tools of economic pressure. From the 1980s to the 2010s, the US increasingly used secondary sanctions to transform the dollar-based financial system into a powerful instrument for exerting geopolitical pressure and isolating foreign governments and companies.But that seems to be changing now. Tariffs, secondary sanctions and more - the Donald Trump administration has all tried several tricks up its sleeve to browbeat the global economy. But, the world has survived.A recent report by Henrich Foundation notes: “Overwhelming US sanctions power was for many years a strategic substitute for US military power projection, allowing the economic containment of rival states and thereby freeing up military resources for prime theaters such as the Middle East and East Asia.“In both these regions, however, US military power and sanctions power now appear less capable of deterrence than before,” it says.What has changed? Why is the world less affected by US sanctions and what does this mean for India?For decades, the United States relied on its overwhelming ability to impose sanctions as an alternative to projecting military power. Economic restrictions helped Washington contain rival states while allowing it to reserve military resources for strategically important regions, particularly the Middle East and East Asia.Whether it was the 2000s or 2010s, the US used secondary sanctions to compel European banks to comply with restrictions that were targeted at Iran, Sudan and Cuba.It all started with the growing strength of the dollar as part of the integrated global trading system from the 1980s onwards. This raised the economic cost for countries of being cut off from the US dollar system.According to the Henrich Foundation report, “The traded goods share of global GDP rose continuously from 36% of global GDP in 1979 to 55% of global GDP in 2015.”By the late 1990s and the 2000s, the dollar had firmly established itself not just as the world's leading reserve currency, but also an important invoicing currency, borrowing currency, source of liquidity and vehicle currency for foreign investment.The United States also benefited from a substantial imbalance in economic power. Its position gave it a significant advantage over countries targeted by sanctions, which had relatively few options to retaliate against Washington's economic measures.A further factor underpinning US sanctions’ power was the period of relative macroeconomic stability that lasted from the mid-1980s until the mid-2010s.According to Henrich, from 2010 onward, a fourth pillar further enhanced the US ability to target the main commodity export of its rivals: oil production.“Thanks to easy financing conditions, the US experienced a domestic shale oil boom and became a net exporter of fossil fuels,” its report says.Fundamentally, as the risk of sanctions has become more persistent, countries have grown increasingly interested in protecting themselves against their exposure to the US dollar.The Henrich report notes since 2017, and particularly after the “Liberation Day” tariffs that were introduced in spring 2025, US tariff measures have prompted changes in the configuration of global supply chains.“The growing use of export controls on all kinds of strategic items - semiconductors and chipmaking equipment, AI technology, rare earths, and so on - is driving companies and governments to invest in domestic production capacity and in stronger alliance networks that can secure these technologies,” the report says.“On the whole, the world economy has weathered the impact of trade conflict and economic warfare,” it adds.In fact, the report cautions that recent economic research indicates that these developments may weaken US power more severely and more quickly than measures of its overall control over global networks might imply.One of the biggest examples of the diminishing power of America’s secondary sanctions is the strong shadow tanker fleet that continues to globally transport Russian energy supplies.US sanctions against Iran and Venezuela during the 2010s, followed by the coordinated G7 measures against Russia in the early 2020s, progressively excluded several major oil-producing countries from the unrestricted international market centred on the Brent crude benchmark.However, these restrictions did not eliminate the trade in oil. Instead, they redirected it towards alternative channels that are harder to monitor. The global oil market has, in effect, split into two segments: a largely unrestricted market accounting for most oil traded internationally, and a smaller but still substantial “shadow” market created by sanctions.“To supply the growing shadow market in oil, an entire ecosystem of tankers, shipping companies, and insurers formed. Many of this network’s participants function to facilitate the joint trade of Venezuela, Iran, and Russia, while supplying oil importers such as China, India, Türkiye, Vietnam, Indonesia, and others,” the report says.“Despite voluminous and regular new sanctions designations on these ships, companies, and facilitators, secondary sanctions have not proven capable of meaningfully reducing or permanently denting this gray oil market,” the report adds.Not only that, Russia is actively exploring the Northern Sea Route for its exports.And then come China and Iran.China’s restrictions on rare earth exports, alongside Iran’s capacity to disrupt shipping in the Gulf and interfere with oil and gas production in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, have given these countries economic tools with which to push back directly against the US.“This development was apparent in October 2025, when a Chinese embargo on its rare earth exports forced Donald Trump to accept a tariff truce in the Sino-US trade war. Faced with growing shortages in US manufacturing and the defense industry, Trump agreed at an important meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at Busan in South Korea not to impose new export controls and to revert several recent controls on chip exports to China,’ the report explains.Caught off guard by US sanctions targeting its telecommunications sector and chipmakers in 2018–2019, Beijing has spent considerable effort developing a strategy to retaliate with economic pressure during Donald Trump’s second term. Since then, China has further expanded its permanent export-control machinery, ensuring that it can keep this option available for use whenever necessary.“Any significant new US export controls and tariffs risk reactivating a painful Chinese response. But because this stability rests on a commitment to US abstinence from serious secondary sanctions against Chinese entities, Washington’s freedom of maneuver in this space is reduced in the long run,” the report says.Iran, too, has demonstrated its capacity to affect the US economy in 2026. The impact is less immediate and operates through indirect channels, but restrictions on traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have triggered a global fuel crisis with consequences for the American economy.Despite being a major exporter of fossil fuels, the US remains vulnerable to oil price shocks in particular product markets.Iran’s strategic position in the Strait of Hormuz, combined with Russia’s natural gas exports, gives the two countries control over approximately 42% of the global natural gas market, covering both liquefied natural gas and supplies transported through pipelines.China, Iran and Russia have built up countervailing economic leverage across a range of critical resources, from rare earth metals to natural gas and petroleum products. Although these capabilities do not eliminate the considerable geoeconomic power that the US Treasury retains through secondary sanctions, they have made it harder for Washington to deploy economic coercion without facing resistance.Yet another important point to note is that the effects of US sanctions are increasingly being felt in the Treasury market as foreign governments are reducing their exposure to US debt.The report points out that foreign official holdings fell 8.4% from $4.24 trillion in January 2021 to $3.87 trillion in December 2025, while China has more than halved its holdings over the past decade. This has given Beijing greater scope to use Treasury sales to pressure Washington.The trend accelerated after the US attack on Iran, with overseas public-sector holdings dropping 6.3% between February and August 2026, including a 31% fall in short-term Treasury bills to $312 billion.For India, the news is mixed. Sanctions are seen as an economic leverage, but India has till now not finalised a trade deal with the US, insisting on a competitive advantage. It has also not stopped buying Russian crude. Resilience in exports through diversified markets and trade agreements has also helped in India.According to Vivek Iyer, Partner and Financial Services Risk Advisory Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat, India is moderately exposed to sanctions pressure, and in a few concentrated areas.“The thesis that alternative networks blunt sanctions mostly helps countries that are themselves sanctioned, like Russia and Iran. India is a third country. Its banks, exporters and refiners rely heavily on dollar clearing and US markets, so a secondary-sanctions threat still works on India even if it has weakened against Russia,” he tells TOI.Energy remains the biggest exposure. The new Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act allows the US to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas. India, which takes more Russian crude than any country except China, is one of them.On October 16, Trump waived sections 112 and 113 and most of the Act's sanctions provisions, but that waiver is discretionary and can be reversed. Russia's share of India's crude imports was roughly 56% at its height and fell to about 35% in September.And there is a past precedent to US pressure when Trump imposed a 25% penal tariff on India for its Russian oil purchases. India did not stop buying Russian crude oil due to tariffs, but subsequent sanctions on Russian oil majors did force it to recalibrate oil procurement strategy.Yet, the US needs India both strategically and in oil markets.Ajay Srivastava, founder, Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) believes that India remains vulnerable at both the company and country levels.“The risk has already shaped India’s energy choices. India stopped buying Iranian crude and previously cut back on Venezuelan oil to avoid US sanctions. The Russian oil tariff showed how a dispute over energy imports can reach Indian exporters with no connection to the oil trade,” he tells TOI.Yet, to a point tougher US sanctions may benefit India.“For the US, the costs show up as higher oil prices (the Rosneft/Lukoil sanctions precipitated an 8% increase in global Brent crude oil prices), tariffs paid by US consumers, and faster growth of alternative payment systems. For India, the possible gains include discounted crude, more trade settled in rupees, GIFT City attracting flows that are being diverted, and better market access if it lines up with the US,” Vivek Iyer tells TOI.
Article Summary: For decades, the United States relied on its overwhelming ability to impose sanctions as an alternative to projecting military power. Tariffs, secondary sanctions and more - the Donald Trump administration has all tried several tricks up its sleeve to browbeat the global economy. But, the world has survived.

Article Title: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney dies at 95; started global chain with $600 loan from mother
Article Text:
Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney.

Who was Dan Carney?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wichita State pays tribute

Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney, who turned a $600 loan from his mother into one of the world's biggest pizza chains alongside his brother Frank, has died at the age of 95.Carney died peacefully on November 13, surrounded by his family, according to an obituary published by his family. No cause of death was disclosed. The New York Post reported his death on Monday, citing the obituary.Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University.The venture took off despite pizza being relatively unfamiliar to many American diners at the time. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.In 1977, PepsiCo acquired Pizza Hut for $300 million. Frank, who had served as the company's CEO, left the position in 1980. He died in December 2020 at the age of 82 after battling pneumonia.Born in Kansas City, Missouri, Carney grew up in a large family and was one of 12 siblings, according to the NYP. He graduated from Wichita State University in 1953 with a bachelor's degree in business administration.He subsequently served two years in the US Air Force as a first lieutenant before returning to his academic pursuits.He received his master's degree in 2004, 51 years after completing his undergraduate studies.Carney married his childhood sweetheart, Beverly Singleton, in February 1954. The couple had six children and 12 grandchildren. Beverly died in 1998. Carney later married Gayla Coulter in 2001, and she survives him.Beyond his business career, Carney was involved in philanthropy and served as chairman of the board of the Cerebral Palsy Research Foundation of Kansas for 50 years.His obituary described him as a leader known for his integrity, generosity and commitment to mentoring others.“Dan was revolutionary in the franchise world,” the obituary said, adding that he was an investor not just in businesses but also in people.Wichita State University, Carney's alma mater, also paid tribute to the entrepreneur, recalling his contribution to the institution and the wider community.In a Facebook post on Monday, the university described him as an entrepreneur, philanthropist and proud Shocker whose impact would be felt for generations.The university also highlighted his humility, wisdom and belief in giving back, saying his mentorship had shaped the lives of students and colleagues.The original Pizza Hut building, where the brothers launched their business, has been preserved on the Wichita State campus. It now houses the Pizza Hut Museum, which opened to the public in 2018.Carney had attended the museum's opening and described seeing the original building as a humbling experience, according to a Wichita State University press release.
Article Summary: Carney and his brother Frank founded Pizza Hut in 1958 in Wichita, Kansas, when Dan was 26. The brothers borrowed $600 from their mother to set up their first restaurant, which opened near Wichita State University. Within a year, the brothers began franchising the business, which subsequently expanded into an international restaurant chain.

Article Title: US reveals how Megaspeed came under scrutiny and landed on Nvidia's 'no sell' list in 2025
Article Text:
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia's partnership with Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed hit a roadblock in June 2025, when the chipmaker put it on its "no sell" list. The decision came after US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner, according to information released by the US commerce and justice departments on Monday.The US investigation, however, had started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to the possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.The commerce department approached Nvidia in May 2025, seeking records of direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. A month later, the company found itself on Nvidia's restricted sales list, the two departments said in a joint statement.The agencies said the probe was triggered by suspicious activity detected through monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion."After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the department of commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations," the agencies said, as cited by Reuters.The investigation moved beyond records and sales checks in June 2025, when US agents travelled to Megaspeed's premises with Singaporean law enforcement officials. They carried out an "on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed" and questioned Alice Huang, who was then the company's chief executive.The Justice Department subsequently took charge of the criminal investigation into Megaspeed, following the enforcement action.The two departments said they were making details of the case public despite the usual practice of not commenting on ongoing investigations, citing public interest.Megaspeed's dealings with Nvidia are not the only aspect of the company drawing suspicion. Its former executive Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman, has also come under scrutiny, with some US authorities suspecting links to Chinese espionage efforts. However, Beijing has continued to refute the allegations.The allegations gained attention following reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12. en unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang formally left the company on August 30, 2025. It also maintained that it had conducted a "legitimate and lawful business."Singapore's government had said last week that Alice Huang previously held three key positions at Megaspeed — chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.Police found insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to suspected false declarations over server purchases. However, they warned her for knowingly providing inaccurate information that played down her role in the company.Singapore has barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country. Investigations involving Megaspeed and six other individuals are still underway, the home affairs ministry said.Meanwhile, Singapore's government said on Monday that it had agreed to continue discussions with Washington over the company.
Article Summary: N Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed in June 2025. US investigators sought details of Nvidia's direct and indirect sales to its Asia-Pacific partner. US investigation started much earlier, in 2024, after authorities flagged suspicious activity linked to possible diversion of sensitive semiconductors.

Article Title: Trump’s Nvidia stake grew to as much as $62 million: Report
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Trump's Nvidia stake

White House response to questions over Trump's Nvidia holdings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘She may not be a spy,’ says Trump

US President Donald Trump has stood by Nvidia’s former boss Jensen Huang despite a string of personal scandals, including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.But there is another Nvidia connection drawing attention: Trump's own stock portfolio.His investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year, with financial disclosures suggesting that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million.The disclosures put Trump's Nvidia holdings under the spotlight as the company grapples with controversy surrounding Huang's resignation and its business dealings with China.Trump’s Nvidia holdings, estimated at between $615,000 and $1.3 million at the end of 2024, rose to as much as $62 million within the last year, according to financial disclosures reviewed by The Washington Post. However, these filings do not include trades made over the past two months, so the latest value of his holdings could be even higher, The Independent reported.But the value of his holdings is only part of the picture. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.A CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures found that his accounts had bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times.The transactions were worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million.The exact size of Trump's current stake, however, remains unclear. His disclosures report investments in broad dollar-value ranges rather than the actual number of shares held. Based on the holdings reported in August, his Nvidia investment would have been worth between $4.5 million and $57.7 million by midday Monday, when the stock was trading at around $157.The latest disclosures do not capture transactions from the past two months, making it difficult to establish how much Nvidia stock Trump currently owns.Trump's investment accounts sold between $500,001 and $1 million worth of Nvidia shares on May 18, the first Monday after his return from a China visit with Huang. The sale was part of a wider trading spree, with Trump disclosing more than 21,000 trades in 2025, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.The scale of Trump's Nvidia investments has also raised questions about his financial interests in the company, particularly given his close relationship with Huang and his administration's decisions on export controls.The administration has opened the door for Nvidia to do business in China, while Trump has repeatedly defended its approach to export restrictions against criticism. These decisions have come under scrutiny as the company faces questions over its China-related business and the allegations surrounding Huang.White House officials have repeatedly maintained that Trump does not personally select or trade individual stocks. The president has also rejected calls to sell his stock holdings.According to the White House, Trump's assets are held in a trust managed by his children, while independent financial managers handle his investment portfolio.Trump has also appeared to question his administration's assessment of Alice Huang's alleged links to Chinese intelligence.“I don’t know that she’s a spy at all. Nobody's proven that,” he told reporters outside the White House on Monday. “He probably shouldn’t have been doing, on a personal basis, what he did. You know, from — who knows? That's a different story. But nobody's proven that she's a spy. She may not be a spy,” he said.Nvidia shares were trading at around $157.72 on Monday, down more than 3.1% during the day. The decline came as investors reacted to Huang's resignation ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings call scheduled for Tuesday.Huang stepped down last Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, who is suspected of being a spy.
Article Summary: Trump's investments in the AI chipmaker have grown sharply over the past year. Financial disclosures suggest that his stake could be worth as much as $62 million. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have been actively buying and selling Nvidia shares.

Article Title: Oil prices fall as rising supply outweighs Middle East tensions and fears of tanker attacks
Article Text:
Oil eases as Middle East supply worry subsides

Oil prices plunged marginally on Tuesday, with the prospect of a global supply surplus taking precedence over concerns about attacks on oil tankers in the Middle East. The possibility of rising supplies has weighed on the market even as tensions continue to threaten energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the region.WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents, or 0.62%, to $91.87. Prices were quoted with a 10-minute delay.Earlier on Friday, the International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year. The agency attributed this outlook to Middle East exports recovering at a faster pace than global oil demand, despite attacks on shipping.However, the security situation in the region remains a concern. Attacks on energy infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty around a major global oil-export route.Though, geopolitical concerns are still present, they no longer having as much influence on prices as the supply outlook.Meanwhile, OPEC held a virtual meeting on Monday to discuss its assessment of members' maximum sustainable production capacity.The review is an important exercise as it will help establish OPEC+ production quotas for 2027 and subsequent years.The broader OPEC+ alliance, which also includes oil-producing countries led by Russia, is set to meet on November 29. The meeting will focus on deciding the group's oil output policy for 2027.In another development, US crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 276.4 million barrels last week, marking their lowest level since August 1982, according to Department of Energy data.The latest reduction is part of an agreement by the US to release 172 million barrels of oil from the reserve.
Article Summary: WTI crude was down 48 cents, or 0.56%, at $85.24, while Brent crude declined 57 cents,or 0.62%, to $91.87. International Energy Agency said that global oil market would move back into surplus in the fourth quarter of this year.

Article Title: Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang’s return: Report
Article Text:
Jensen Huang (right) with Alice Huang. She is rumoured to be a Chinese spy
